name: Responsive Cover
idea: Two broad textile folds make a shared interior and turn their meeting into an upward opening.
construction: Two substantial, asymmetric curved panels, not an arch with a separate figure.
The space held between the panels is part of the construction.
risk: The organic embrace can suggest a general care charity; the covering is abstract.
why: Tested as a research-led hypothesis before shortlist selection.

name: Coupled Fabric
idea: Separate textile lengths become one woven dwelling through a visible over-and-under relationship.
construction: Broad orthogonal textile lengths turn around a shared center.
Alternating interruptions suggest coupling rather than extra ornament.
risk: Its woven logic can look like an industrial or technology monogram.
why: Tested as a research-led hypothesis before shortlist selection.

name: Processional Court
idea: A generous open perimeter brings entering and a common interior into one plan-like sign.
construction: One continuous court perimeter with a broad unclosed threshold.
Two interior panels establish rhythm without drawing worshippers.
risk: Could read as a maze, venue plan, or a closed institution; literal sanctuary access is not implied.
why: Tested as a research-led hypothesis before shortlist selection.

name: Returning Thanks
idea: A continuous spatial gesture enters, gathers, and turns outward: thanksgiving as a response rather than a gate icon.
construction: A single broad path folds from enclosure into an open outward return.
No discrete doorway, arrow, person, or musical symbol is added.
risk: A continuous return can read as a letter or a general wayfinding symbol.
why: Tested as a research-led hypothesis before shortlist selection.

name: Held Light
idea: A substantial surrounding form gives a white interior room to open upward, exploring presence through attention to space.
construction: Two curved masses hold one continuous white interior, open at top and base.
The opening is material absence; it is not labeled as God.
risk: A vessel, flame, or seed is an alternative reading. Divine presence cannot be reduced to a white aperture.
why: Tested as a research-led hypothesis before shortlist selection.

name: Room in the Veil
idea: The meeting of folded screens makes a luminous room rather than a façade; the unseen interior becomes the focal point.
construction: Offset screen planes hold a larger unfilled chamber and a secondary inner fold.
The geometry is a contemporary spatial abstraction, not a historical reconstruction.
risk: A portal or architectural app symbol may dominate; extra inner detail may weaken the essential idea.
why: Tested as a research-led hypothesis before shortlist selection.
